title: Prescale the search tier ahead of traffic with Minimum Search VCUs for Elasticsearch Serverless
summary: Set a Minimum Search VCU floor on Elasticsearch Serverless 30 minutes before traffic arrives, so the search tier is scaled before the queries land.
body_markdown:
[Elasticsearch](https://elastic.co/elasticsearch)[Serverless](https://www.elastic.co/cloud/serverless) scales the search tier as traffic changes. When you know that demand is coming for a sale or a newsletter, or at the start of the business day, Minimum Search VCUs (virtual compute units) lets you scale the search tier ahead of time.


With Minimum Search VCUs, you choose a minimum Search VCU for your Elasticsearch Serverless project. Check your existing Search VCU usage to determine how much search capacity you want provisioned before traffic arrives. The search tier scales to at least that level, and[autoscaling](https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/autoscaling) continues to increase capacity as needed for search power or searchable data, as well as for search load.


## When to prescale the Elasticsearch Serverless search tier


Some search demand has a shape that you can anticipate; for example:


-


**Promotional events.** A retail catalog has a steady baseline, but traffic jumps when a sale email goes out. You raise the minimum before the email is sent, so the search tier is scaled ahead of the expected traffic.


-


**Predictable operating hours.** Query


volume follows a daily or shift-based pattern, busy through the workday or warehouse shift and then quieter overnight. You raise the minimum before the busy period and lower it when the shift ends.


## How many Minimum Search VCUs should you set?


Choose a minimum between your observed baseline and your observed peak Search VCU usage. Start with the **Usage and performance** chart in the Elastic Cloud console, which shows Search VCU usage over the last 10 days. Compare your baseline and peak usage, and choose a minimum that prepares your search tier for predictable demand, keeping in mind:


-


**Scale ahead of demand.** Approximately 30–60 minutes before incoming requests, set the minimum.


-


**Use your own usage as a guide.** The settings page shows the last 10 days of Search VCU usage, alongside the minimum that you’re configuring (drawn as a line on the chart). This helps you compare your chosen level with the search tier that your project has already used.


-


**Autoscaling stays on.** When needed, Search VCUs can still rise above the lowest number that you provisioned.


## How much do Minimum Search VCUs cost?


While Minimum Search VCUs is enabled, you pay for at least that many Search VCUs, including when search load is below the minimum or idle. When autoscaling adds Search VCUs above the minimum, you pay for those additional Search VCUs for as long as they stay provisioned. As search load decreases, Search VCUs can scale back down toward (but not below) the configured minimum.Minimum Search VCUs stays at the level you set until you lower or disable it in project settings or until you change it through the API.


## Set Minimum Search VCUs in the Elastic Cloud console


To configure Minimum Search VCUs:


1. Log in to the[Elastic Cloud console](https://cloud.elastic.co/) , and open the Elasticsearch Serverless project.


2. On the project overview, go to the **Usage and performance** tab and review the **VCUs** chart. The **Search** series shows Search VCU usage for your project.


3. Select **Manage minimum search VCUs** on the VCUs chart, or go to the **Project** **settings** tab.


4. Enable **Minimum Search VCUs** . The page shows up to the last 10 days of Search VCU usage. with the minimum drawn as a line, for comparison.


5. Enter a whole number of **Minimum Search VCUs** , and select **Save** .


6. Review the confirmation, including the Search VCU number and its billing implications, and then confirm the change.


After you enable the setting, the **Search VCU** chart in the Elastic Cloud console includes **Minimum Search VCUs** as a line, so you can easily compare your configured minimum with actual usage:


When you no longer need Minimum Search VCUs, you can disable it in the project settings.


### Set or disable Minimum Search VCUs through the Elastic Cloud Serverless API


You can set Minimum Search VCUs through the[Elastic Cloud Serverless API](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elastic-cloud-serverless/operation/operation-createelasticsearchproject#operation-createelasticsearchproject-body-application-json-search_lake-min_search_vcu) . See the[documentation](https://www.elastic.co/docs/deploy-manage/deploy/elastic-cloud/project-settings#minimum-search-vcus) for more details. When you no longer need Minimum Search VCUs, you can disable it via the[API](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elastic-cloud-serverless/operation/operation-patchelasticsearchproject#operation-patchelasticsearchproject-body-application-json-search_lake-min_search_vcu) .
